newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee firm as speculators sell dollars.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee firm as speculators sell dollars.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee, which took an early tumble on Friday, was stronger after speculators began to sell dollars when the local currency passed the psychological barrier of 57.80, dealers said.
At 0500 GMT the rupee was at 57.67 to the dollar after opening at 57.75 and rising to 57.82 on speculative buying, they said. The rupee closed at 57.74 on Thursday.
"Early speculation pushed up the dollar but sellers came in after the rate moved over 57.80," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates were at 12.25 percent after opening at 13 percent, dealers said.
"There is no reason for money rates to go up because the market is well offered," said one dealer.
